articles.title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded
articles.description: Nicola Shaw, who has led the company since 2022, will step down in January, it is announced.
articles.summary: Nicola Shaw had been criticised over Yorkshire Water's pay and performance Yorkshire Water's chief executive has announced she is to step down, just 24 hours after the company was given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency Nicola Shaw, who has led the firm since 2022, will leave…
key_points: In a statement on Friday, Shaw said it had been a "privilege" to lead the company but that it was "the right time" to leave her post.
Shaw has faced criticism in recent years, including for taking £1.3m in undisclosed payments between 2023 and 2025, while the company has come under scrutiny for its performance.
On Thursday, the Environment Agency gave the firm one star out of four - its lowest possible rating - meaning Yorkshire Water was classed as a "poorly performing company".

articles.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
articles.description: Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI own search summaries were affecting ad revenue.
articles.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has backed the company's massive spending on AI.
key_points: Google-owner Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after it revealed its own artificial intelligence (AI) summaries were hitting search advertising revenue.

Chief business officer Philipp Schindler said Google's "AI mode", where it answers questions conversationally, was eating into the money it makes from ads which appear next to results to traditional search questions.
Yet, Schindler said he felt "very good about our trajectory" with an AI-focused version of the search engine.

articles.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history
articles.description: Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what could be the largest hack in history.
key_points: The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".
Early checks show the incident may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025 , to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
